conclusion: Without block reward, starting mistake rate 0.7/0.5 beat 0.3; adding block reward 0.5 collapsed performance despite high collected block reward. Run 1eb96584a93f43c2a5e3148ec35b17fe is mislabeled 30p but raw start_mistake_rate is 0.7, so it is not evidence for a 0.3 block-reward cell.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Establish the no-block-reward control at a 0.7 initial heuristic mistake rate.

results_insights.insight: The 70% mistake-rate control reached 26.83% average win rate.
The weakest matchup won only 2%.
Combined-X reached 41% over 10.9-move games.
The combined-X comparison had moderate episode duration.

reasoning: A high initial opponent mistake rate supported moderate average learning without block reward.
The low 2% floor shows substantial remaining side asymmetry.
This is the within-sweep control; stochastic variation remains because there are no same-setting replications.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Test whether lowering initial heuristic mistakes from 0.7 to 0.5 improves no-block-reward learning.

results_insights.insight: Average win rate was nearly unchanged versus 0.7 (26.33% versus 26.83%).
The floor declined from 2% to zero.
Combined-X improved from 41% to 60%, over 10.87-move games.
Episode duration closely matched the 0.7 control.

reasoning: Lowering start mistakes redistributed competence rather than improving the average.
Combined-X benefited, but a different zero-win matchup worsened the robustness floor.
The comparison changes one logged knob, though unreplicated stochastic variation remains.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Test whether a still-stronger initial heuristic at 0.3 mistakes improves no-block-reward learning.

results_insights.insight: Average performance collapsed to 12.67%.
The floor remained zero.
Combined-X fell to zero wins, over 8.08-move games.
The zero-win combined-X games were shorter than higher-mistake controls.

reasoning: Starting against the stronger 0.3-mistake opponent was too difficult for this curriculum.
The zero combined-X result explains much of the aggregate regression.
The one-knob sweep supports the trend, but each setting has only one stochastic run.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Test whether adding a 0.5 block reward improves the 0.7-mistake curriculum control.

results_insights.insight: Average win rate collapsed from 26.83% without block reward to 2.5%.
Worst rate was 1%.
The agent collected substantial shaped block reward despite poor evaluator wins.
Defensive-X games became long while win rate was only 6%.

reasoning: A 0.5 block reward dominated the objective and harmed actual winning competence.
High collected block reward alongside 2.5% wins suggests reward misalignment.
Defense weight also differs from the no-block controls, but shaping coefficient is zero; single-seed uncertainty remains.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Within the 0.5 block-reward regimen, test whether lowering start mistakes from 0.7 to 0.5 helps.

results_insights.insight: Average increased slightly from 2.5% to 3.33% but remained extremely poor.
The floor fell to zero.
Mean block reward rose while evaluator competence remained poor.
Very long defensive-X games yielded only 8% wins.

reasoning: Changing start mistakes did not correct the severe 0.5 block-reward misalignment.
Higher collected block rewards without evaluator gains reinforce reward hacking/misalignment concerns.
The small average difference is within plausible stochastic noise.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Nominally test the 0.3-mistake block-reward condition, while preserving the raw fact that params/start_mistake_rate is actually 0.7 and therefore makes this a mislabeled replication.

results_insights.insight: The mislabeled 0.7 replication reached 4.83%, still extremely poor.
Worst rate was 1%.
Mean block reward closely matched the earlier 0.7 run's 0.23154.
Defensive-X was 14% over 32.76-move games.
The paired episode-length metric confirms the 32.76-move defensive-X evaluation.

reasoning: Raw parameters prove this is a 0.7 replication, not the 0.3 condition stated in its run name.
Its poor average replicates the central result that 0.5 block reward harms winning competence.
The modest difference versus the other 0.7 run is consistent with stochastic variation.
